claims.text: The initial material is cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance at high temperature.
The Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy family can combine strength and plasticity.
The proposed intervention is an approximately 100 nm dense Al2O3 coating deposited by atomic layer deposition.
The ALD coating will form a stable, continuous alumina scale on HfNbTaTiZr during exposure at about 1000 °C in air.
The alumina coating will act as an oxygen-diffusion barrier.
Blocking oxygen diffusion will prevent oxidative degradation of the underlying HfNbTaTiZr alloy.
The protective coating will limit formation of detrimental oxides that would otherwise damage the alloy microstructure and mechanical performance.
After exposure at 1000 °C in air for up to approximately 100 hours, coated samples will have significantly lower oxidation weight gain than uncoated samples.
After the specified exposure, coated samples will have a thinner and more uniform oxide scale than uncoated samples.
The coated alloy will retain room-temperature tensile ductility within the untreated alloy's 8–16% range.
The coated alloy will retain high-temperature yield strength within the untreated alloy's 163–530 MPa range.
The prediction is bounded to approximately 1000 °C air exposure for no more than about 100 hours under quasi-static tensile loading.
The prediction does not cover long-term cyclic thermal exposure.
Long-term coating adhesion, thermal-cycling stability, and coating-induced surface stress effects remain uncertain.
